reader.title: Killing of Dolly Durand
chips: Lynching of any race (not in the anti-Black count)
bases: A band of armed men (six, per the San Antonio dispatch) shot a state's witness in a murder trial while he slept, the papers inferring revenge for his testimony; no paper gives the race of the victim or the attackers or any racial motive (A6, A8).

Durand was shot dead by a party of six men acting without any authority (A6, A8), but the only motive the papers give is their own inference of revenge for, or prevention of, his testimony (A6, A8), and nothing in the coverage says he was Black or that the killing was framed as punishment or racial.
The local Evening Light (A6) and the San Antonio dispatch in the Dallas Herald (A8) independently agree that Durand was shot dead while asleep outdoors at night, his neck broken and body riddled.

summary.text: The killing of Dolly Durand was the shooting of a state's witness in a Texas murder trial by unidentified men as he slept outdoors near the Ingle settlement, reported from San Antonio, on the night of Saturday, September 30, 1882.
No one was reported arrested, and the papers treated the killing as revenge for his testimony against John Lyons, whom a San Antonio jury had just acquitted.

In September 1882 John Lyons was tried in the district court at San Antonio for complicity in the 1881 killing of Dick McCoy at Altito pasture in LaSalle county, where McCoy had been riding with a party hunting stolen cattle.

Durand testified for the state that he had been with the Wright party at the pen, that James Wright and his brother shot McCoy, and that "defendant fired" next, while he himself "took no part in the fighting."
A defense witness, an officer, testified that Durand had been arrested on suspicion of killing McCoy, was under indictment for horse-stealing, and had been promised help with his troubles.
Durand then left San Antonio during the trial, and a witness testified that Dimmitt county sheriff Joe Tumlinson and others had offered him money to go, which Tumlinson and the others denied.

The Lyons jury returned a verdict of "not guilty," the cases of his co-defendants were continued because of Durand's absence, and the Evening Light reported efforts to find "the witness who fled the town" and to prosecute those who had bribed him.
According to the Evening Light, Durand was tending horses a few miles from the ranch on the Ingle settlement with a man named Jim, and was said to be on his way to San Antonio.
While the two slept out that night, "some persons" stole upon them and shot Durand in the neck, killing him instantly, then riddled his body from so close that his clothes caught fire.
Several shots were fired at his companion, who ran and escaped unhurt.
A San Antonio dispatch gave the hour as 1 o'clock at night and said "a party of six men rode up" to where he lay asleep in the woods.
No report of an inquest, arrests or prosecution for the killing appears in the coverage.

The San Antonio Evening Light broke the news on October 2 under the headline "MURDERED ASLEEP!", called the shooting the killers' "foul work," and said it was "supposed" to be revenge for his evidence or a way to prevent further evidence.

The San Antonio dispatch printed in the Dallas Daily Herald on October 3 was harsher toward the victim, calling Durand "a notorious thief" believed to be McCoy's murderer who had turned state's witness "to swear the lives of others away," while stating that he was "undoubtedly" killed for testifying against Lyons.
The same dispatch ran in the Wheeling Daily Intelligencer on October 5 under the headline "A Dangerous Witness Silenced," with the name printed "Daily Durand."
None of these reports mentioned the race of Durand or of the men who killed him.

accounts.label: Local report (Evening Light)
accounts.gist: On Saturday night 'some persons' stole on Durand and a companion sleeping out near the Ingle settlement, shot him in the neck and riddled his body; the companion escaped. The killing was 'supposed' to be revenge for his evidence or to stop further evidence.

accounts.label: San Antonio wire dispatch
accounts.gist: Six men rode up at 1 a.m. and riddled the sleeping Durand; it calls him a 'notorious thief' believed to be McCoy's murderer and says he was 'undoubtedly' killed for testifying against Lyons.

framing.detail: The San Antonio Evening Light headlined it 'MURDERED ASLEEP!' and called it the killers' 'foul work'.
The Dallas Herald dispatch reported the killing as an assassination of the main witness but described Durand as 'a notorious thief' who turned state's witness 'to swear the lives of others away'.
The Wheeling Intelligencer ran the dispatch under 'A Dangerous Witness Silenced'.
